provenance.purpose: Curated disposition for NECB 2025 Section 8.4 articles that no domain manifest declares: who or what satisfies each one. Consumed by python/scripts/generate_necb_8_4_coverage.py.

categories.engine: satisfied by EnergyPlus itself (physics the simulation engine performs)
categories.modeller: the modeller's or AHJ's responsibility — a scoping or input decision, not software
categories.covered_by: satisfied by named gem code that has not (yet) declared a manifest entry for this article
categories.gap: genuinely uncovered — nothing in the family satisfies it

provenance.rules: Every entry needs a rationale. A disposition is a claim of RESPONSIBILITY, not of correctness — the weaker claim is deliberate. Entries are drafts until a named human reviews them; the generator renders drafts distinctly and flags any article that is both dispositioned and declared/cited (conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved).

8.4.6.1.rationale: Part-load curves ARE applied by the efficiency passes: reference boilers and gas furnace coils carry the edition's own FHeatPLC as a Table:Lookup (D-89); DX coils, chillers, air-source heat pumps and service water heaters carry the edition's curve rows. python/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py builds the components, runs the Python appliers and compares the as-applied curves with the published rows (tests/necb/test_necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py is the gate). The condensing-boiler row is not compared: no reference build selects it.
8.4.6.1.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, docs/necb_decisions.md D-08); rationale revised 2026-09-14 for D-89 (Sol's fourth pass), pending re-review

8.4.6.2.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT (D-89): each reference boiler carries its own edition's FHeatPLC through PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR) as a Table:Lookup. The classes stated by a quadratic row (non-condensing in both editions, the 2025 modulating row) use a 169-node grid with a node at PLR 0, sampled maximum error 0.1994 % (non-condensing) and 0.7905 % (2025 modulating) against the exact rational; the 2020 modulating table is carried exactly at its ten printed points from PLR 0.10. As applied, the non-condensing table matches its row at 0.00 % over PLR 0.25-1.0 (python/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py, 2026-09-14). The condensing row is not implemented: no reference rule elects a condensing boiler.
8.4.6.2.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, docs/necb_decisions.md D-08); rationale revised 2026-09-14 for D-89 (Sol's fourth pass), pending re-review

8.4.6.3.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT (D-89): the gas-coil part-load fraction is the atmospheric FHeatPLC through PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), a 100-node Table:Lookup from PLR 0.055 (the first node above EnergyPlus's 0.7 floor on a fuel coil's part-load fraction), sampled maximum error 0.0330 %, with identical coefficients in both editions. As applied it matches the atmospheric row at 0.00 % over PLR 0.25-1.0 (python/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py, 2026-09-14). The modulating furnace class is unreachable and has no representation (a WARNING if ever selected).
8.4.6.3.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, docs/necb_decisions.md D-08); rationale revised 2026-09-14 for D-89 (Sol's fourth pass), pending re-review

8.4.6.4.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT (fixed 2026-07-22): CAP_FT and EIR_FT are the code surfaces exactly (0.01%/0.00%, exact degF->degC transforms — EIR_FT was regenerated from the code after the probe caught the legacy 2011-derived surface deviating 1.95%); the EIR_FPLR/PLF cycling mapping was refit from the code cubic to its structural floor of ~2.0% (was 3.70%), output clamped to [0.7, 1.0]. 8.4.6.5.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT (Scroll + Reciprocating, water-cooled): CAP_FT, EIR_FPLR and EIR_FT all match at 0.00%. EIR_FT is compared against ERRATUM-CORRECTED coefficients: the PRINTED Table 8.4.5.5-C (2020) / 8.4.6.5-C (2025) rows carry single misplaced-decimal defects (Scroll d, Reciprocating b; the printed Reciprocating row yields a physically impossible negative power ratio at the AHRI rating point) — a publication error identical in both editions, NOT an extraction defect; errata proposed to NRC Codes Canada 2026-07-22. The corrections are corroborated EXACTLY by the independent legacy NECB-2011-lineage vendored curves (all six coefficients, <4e-6 relative, both rows). Screw/Centrifugal probed 2026-07-23 (D-13): all six curves EXACT vs the printed rows (not erratum-affected; their imperfect rating-point normalization is legacy-corroborated). Re-probed 2026-09-14 by python/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py: all twelve chiller curves 0.00 %.
8.4.6.5.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, docs/necb_decisions.md D-08)

8.4.6.6.rationale: The reference tower is CoolingTowerSingleSpeed: EnergyPlus computes available capacity with the Merkel effectiveness-NTU physical model, and the class has NO curve fields the FWB polynomial could be installed into. The FWB/FRA polynomial is the DOE-2.1E curve-fit of the SAME physics (identical coefficients in NECB 2020 8.4.5.6 / 2025 8.4.6.6; underlying relation tA = a + b.tR + c.tR2 + d.FRA + e.FRA2 + f.tR.FRA). NUMERIC CROSS-CHECK (rake necb:curves, gated): both formulations anchored at the CTI rating point (78F wb / 10F range / 7F approach) agree exactly there and within 12.7% across the CTI-wet-bulb slice; at colder wet-bulbs the code fit under-predicts available capacity relative to physics (conservative, up to ~2x at 50F wb) — precisely where capacity never binds because the single-speed fan cycles. E+ is the accepted stand-in for this same DOE-2 polynomial in every EnergyPlus-based 90.1 Appendix G tool. Note the reference tower's UA is sized at the builder's Canadian design point (24C wb / 5K approach / 6K range), a capacity-adequacy choice; 8.4.6.6 governs the part-load adjustment SHAPE, which the NTU model provides.
8.4.6.6.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (directed: disposition as engine, backed by the numeric FWB-vs-NTU cross-check)

8.4.6.7.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT: ASHP heating CAP_FTEAS and EIR_FT are the code cubics exactly (0.00%/0.01%, degF->degC univariate transform); EIR_FPLR via the PLF cycling transform within 1.83%. The -10degC cutoff is separately applied per 8.4.5.13. Re-probed 2026-09-14 by python/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.py: CAP_FTEAS 0.00 %, EIR_FT 0.01 %, EIR_FPLR 1.83 %.
8.4.6.7.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, docs/necb_decisions.md D-08)
